questions.prompt: This repo's yes/no question type is called "noul", but Vercel's AI Gateway calls the same primitive "boolean" and rejects "noul". Where does that translation have to happen, and why there?
options: In the harness, before the cases are loaded, so every provider sees one keyword
In the provider adapter, because the difference is a property of the vendor's wire format, not of the question
In the metrics module, because the Brier score cannot handle two keywords
In the CLI, because the CLI is the only place that knows which provider is in use
questions.explain: The keyword a vendor accepts is a property of that vendor's API, so it belongs in that vendor's adapter. That is exactly what `normalise_questions(questions, wire_keyword)` does: it rewrites our canonical {"type": "noul"} into the vendor's keyword when the two differ. If it lived in the harness, the harness would need to know which vendor is in use - that is the opposite of the one-adapter-one-contract design that makes providers interchangeable. The metrics option is wrong because the metrics never see raw wire keywords - `normalise_answers()` has already folded "boolean" into kind="noul" before any metric runs.

questions.prompt: The harness calls provider.decide(state, questions) and nothing else about the provider. What does that buy the repo?
options: It makes every provider return exactly the same answers, so the comparison is meaningless
It lets the battery, the metrics and the swap matrix be written once against a contract instead of once per vendor
It removes the need for a spend cap, because the harness can no longer see the price
It proves the providers are equally good, because a shared contract implies shared quality
questions.explain: The whole point of the contract is that the harness does not know which vendor is behind it. So `build_provider("clef:clef-flash")` and `build_provider("mock")` are interchangeable, and `python -m decisionarena swap --provider a=jev --provider b=clef:clef-flash` is one code path rather than two programs. The first option is wrong: a shared contract standardises the SHAPE of the answer, not its content - the answers are exactly what differs, and that is what gets measured. The spend-cap option is wrong because the harness reads `price_per_mtok` and `estimate_cost()` precisely because the contract exposes them. The last option is nonsense: a shared interface says nothing about quality, which is why the harness has to measure it.

questions.prompt: Provider.estimate_cost() computes: (usage.get("input_tokens") or usage.get("prompt_tokens") or 0) * price_per_mtok / 1_000_000. A provider returns usage = {"prompt_tokens": 500000} and price_per_mtok = 0.042. What is the cost?
questions.explain: 500000 tokens * 0.042 dollars per million tokens / 1000000 = 0.021 dollars. The division by 1_000_000 is what converts "per million tokens" into "per token", and it is the step people forget. The $0.042 option is the cost of one million tokens, not half a million. The $21.00 option forgets the per-million conversion entirely (500000 * 0.042). The $0.000021 option divides by a million twice. The lesson for the harness: money is always reported in USD with the token counts beside it, because a bare dollar figure is impossible to check.

questions.prompt: In this repo, where do the URLs that requests are sent to actually live, and why does that matter for a local model?
options: In the case JSON files, so each battery decides where it runs
In the adapters - JevProvider.URL and ClefProvider.url() - so an adapter that can be pointed at a local server reuses the same client and the same wire format
In the CLI, which passes --url to every provider
In metrics.py, which records the endpoint next to each score
questions.explain: `JevProvider.URL` is the class attribute "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone", and `ClefProvider.url()` builds the Cloudflare path from the account id and model name. Keeping the endpoint in the adapter is what makes a local server possible: laya-lab/README.md describes pointing the same adapter at http://127.0.0.1:8080 instead of the cloud, so the local model is exercised through the real wire format rather than through a special in-process path. The case-JSON option is wrong - cases carry states and questions, never endpoints. The CLI option is wrong - the CLI takes a provider spec like "jev" or "clef:clef-flash", not a URL. The metrics option is wrong - metrics.py never touches the network.
